description.p: A native Spotify client that opens in under a second and stays light on memory and CPU, with themes that take their colours from the song you play.

ul.li: Vinyl theme, the cover spins like a record and the app takes its colours from the song
Play counts, synced lyrics and local files
Shows up as a Spotify Connect device

description.p: Needs Spotify Premium. onify isn't affiliated with Spotify.

screenshot.caption: An album playing with the Vinyl theme

description.p: Much lighter drawing (the background, zoom and scaled screens), Previous and Next work right after opening onify (taskbar buttons, tray and media keys too), playback carries on after the connection drops, and fixed playlist creating, renaming and deleting.

Playlist editing (add, remove, reorder, create, rename, delete), find inside playlists, crossfade, the last song ready to play at startup, Spotify Connect device switching, zoom, a collapsible sidebar, like and menu buttons on songs, latest and popular releases on artist pages, arrows on Home, Previous twice goes back a song, smoother scrolling and page changes, the system's own font, and ARM builds.

Skipping a paused song plays the next one, Previous on the first song starts it over instead of stopping, Copy Song Link works everywhere (it copied "album" from the player), right-clicking the playing song opens its menu, Windows gets smooth wheel scrolling and its own font (Adwaita Sans), and onify is spelled onify everywhere.
Windows: smooth scrolling at the screen's full frame rate, and sharp text on monitors scaled differently from the main one.

A streaming quality setting, instant skips, music that keeps playing when the output device changes, shuffle and repeat that stay on, a clear message for free accounts, and on Windows: snapping, window animations, Windows-style window buttons and a tray icon.
Update checks, an Arch package, and quitting no longer gets stuck behind open dialogs.
